SRH 125/0 v DC, 20 Apr 2024: IPL record powerplay score

long.vo: In twenty thirteen, IPL teams scored under seven an over in the powerplay. In twenty twenty-six, they scored over ten. The first six overs have become a different sport.

We went through every ball of the IPL since twenty thirteen. For almost a decade, the powerplay barely moved, hovering around seven and a half to eight an over. Then, in twenty twenty-three, it took off. Eight point seven. Then nine and a half. And in twenty twenty-six, ten point one.
Look at sixty-run powerplays. In twenty thirteen, barely one innings in twenty got there. By twenty twenty-two, one in seven. In twenty twenty-six, more than half of all innings did.
Eighty or more in the powerplay used to be a freak event. Zero times in twenty thirteen. In twenty twenty-six, it happened seventeen times.
And the record belongs to Sunrisers हैदराबाद: one hundred and twenty-five without loss in six overs, against दिल्ली, in April twenty twenty-four.

scene.note: The highest powerplay score in IPL history

long.vo: So what changed? Here's the twist. Teams aren't losing many more wickets. In twenty thirteen, the powerplay cost two point eight wickets per match. In twenty twenty-six, three point two. Almost the same risk, for three extra runs an over.

Three things drove it. First, the Impact Player rule in twenty twenty-three gave every team an extra batter, so a wicket costs less. Second, a new generation of openers who attack from ball one, like अभिषेक शर्मा and Travis Head. And third, sixes became the plan, not the risk.

Powerplay sixes per match: 1.5 in 2013, 6.2 in 2026

long.vo: Our verdict? The powerplay is no longer about survival. It's where T-twenty matches are won.
Will we see a one-fifty powerplay? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more data stories.
